newsitem.title: GERMANY: Feed rye still flows into German intervention.
newsitem.headline: Feed rye still flows into German intervention.

text.p: Some 22,716 tonnes of feed rye have been offered to German intervention board BLE over the past week after 53,098 tonnes in the previous fortnight, BLE sources said on Monday.
Feed grain buyers' demand for rye had fallen while feed barley demand was holding up, traders said.
Only 9,750 tonnes of barley offers were received after larger volumes were offered in recent weeks.
Low bread wheat and bread rye prices were attracting free market buyers and restricted offers into intervention.
Total offers in the November-May 1996/97 intervention season still lag those in the same 1995/96 period.
Total grain volumes offered by April 11 totalled 953,605 tonnes compared with 1,665,084 tonnes a year earlier.
The April buying-in price for all grains in 245.83 marks.
